caption_en:
120 Christian majority countries. 53 Muslim. 1 Jewish. ✡️

Pew Research Center (2025) looked at 201 countries and territories (100,000+ people) in 2020: Christian majority 120, Muslim 53, no religion 10, Buddhist 7, Hindu 2, Jewish 1.

Pew (2014): 64 of 196 national flags carry a religious symbol. 31 Christian (the Union Jack's crosses, Greece, Norway, Spain...), 21 Muslim (Turkey, Algeria, Brunei, Uzbekistan...), 5 Buddhist or Hindu, 6 other, and 1 Jewish: Israel's Star of David.

A cross or a crescent on a flag doesn't make a country unfree. Laws do.

Send this to someone who thinks one Jewish state is one too many.
caption_he:
120 מדינות עם רוב נוצרי. 53 עם רוב מוסלמי. אחת עם רוב יהודי.
פיו (2025) בדקו 201 מדינות וטריטוריות: רוב נוצרי 120, מוסלמי 53, בלי דת 10, בודהיסטי 7, הינדי 2, יהודי 1.
פיו (2014): ב-64 מתוך 196 דגלים לאומיים יש סמל דתי. 31 נוצריים, 21 מוסלמיים, 5 בודהיסטיים או הינדיים, 6 אחרים, ואחד יהודי: מגן הדוד של ישראל.
צלב או סהר על דגל לא הופכים מדינה ללא חופשית. חוקים כן.

Sources: Pew Research Center, "The number of Christian-majority countries fell between 2010 and 2020" (2025); Pew Research Center, "64 countries have religious symbols on their national flags" (2014).

lines.line: One hundred and twenty Christian majority countries. How many Jewish ones?
Pew counted two hundred and one countries and territories.
Christian majority: one hundred and twenty.
No religion: ten. Buddhist: seven. Hindu: two.
Sixty four national flags carry a religious symbol.
Thirty one have a cross, like Britain, Greece and Norway.
Twenty one have a Muslim symbol, like Turkey and Algeria.
And one flag has a Star of David.
One Jewish majority country. One Jewish flag.
A cross or a crescent on a flag doesn't make a country unfree. Laws do.
So when someone says the world has one Jewish state too many, ask them:
